processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene (process control reagent, used to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Elemental powders of Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C (99.2% pure) taken in the Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 proportion, milled in a planetary ball mill (Retsch PM 400/2) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; WC vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (35 h milled powder encapsulated in a quartz tube back filled with argon)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 35 h milled sample annealed for 1 h at 800 °C as part of the thermal-stability series (400, 500, 600 and 800 °C), followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase structure: BCC (ferrite) as major phase together with partially ordered B2-type, γ-brass type and Fe5Si3-type silicide. At 800 °C no new phase change occurred relative to the milled powder but the amount of the B2-type phase increased.

phases_present.crystal_structure: Fe5Si3 type (hP16); a = b = 0.667 nm, c = 0.468 nm

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku X-ray diffractometer, Cu-Kα source, 40 kV, 15 mA, scan rate 5° min-1
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, ex-situ on powders annealed at R.T., 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C; the 800 °C pattern is shown in Fig. 5(f).
characterization_methods.purpose: To follow the phase evolution / thermal stability of the milled powder after annealing at increasing temperatures.
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 800 °C no new phase change occurred relative to the milled powder but the amount of B2-type phase increased; Fe5Si3-type silicide, formed at 600 °C, grows further up to 800 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GSAS-II; pseudo-Voigt profile; Chebyschev-I background with 10 coefficients
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 800 °C annealed powder; refinement quality wR = 2.84, GoF = 1.29, χ² = 1.67
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine phase fraction, lattice parameter, volume and crystallite size of the phases present in the 800 °C annealed sample.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature 800 °C (1073 K); composition Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (mole fractions Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.10, C = 0.01); Pressure = 100000 Pa; System size = 1.0 mol.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Some difference exists between the experimental and CALPHAD-predicted phases; this was attributed to using the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

unmapped_findings: The 800 °C annealed specimen is a loose powder used to assess thermal stability / phase evolution; it was not consolidated by SPS, so the mechanical properties reported for the SPSed pellet (microhardness ~7.8 ± 0.3 GPa, elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa, compressive strength 2046 ± 160 MPa, ductility ~19%) do not apply to this sample state.
At 800 °C annealing, no new phase change occurred compared with the lower annealing temperatures, but the phase fraction of the B2-type phase increased (B2 = 40.00% at 800 °C).
Rietveld volumes of the 800 °C annealed phases (Table 4): BCC 23.39 Å³, γ-brass type 663.05 Å³, B2 24.13 Å³ and Fe5Si3 type 180.31 Å³.
The 35 h milled powder was annealed in a quartz tube back-filled with argon and then water quenched.
